name: jsdotnet
description: The jsdotnet plugin marketplace: the devbook knowledge convention and the delivery flow, as agents, skills, instruction files, and hooks authored once and read by both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.

plugins.name: delivery
plugins.description: The host-neutral delivery engine: 16 flow-* staged procedures, 2 shared phases, 7 scheduled automations, and the pull-request lane, sequenced by the flow-runner agent through a closed set of extension points — spec, implement, verify, app.start, qa.run and deliver as services, session.start, flow.start, data.prepare, docs.update and flow.end as chores — with human gates a repository adds but never removes, and a run surface resolved from the live tool list so none is a normal outcome. Bindings, extensions, policy, and gates are declared per repository in .github/ai-agent-stack.json.

plugins.name: delivery-canvas
plugins.description: A render surface: a Mermaid diagram viewer and a Markdown document viewer, shown live beside the files they were written from. Implements one surface capability group — render (render_diagram, render_markdown) — with push/replace navigation and a history the Back button walks, as an MCP server for hosts that speak MCP and as two canvases for hosts with a canvas panel, from one copy of each page. Tracks no runs and exports nothing; declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: delivery-collector
plugins.description: A headless run surface: where a run becomes recorded rather than watched. An MCP server implementing two surface capability groups — lifecycle (open_dashboard, start_run, record_prompt, set_run_context, update_stage, finish_run, list_runs, get_run) and export (export_report) — keeping stage status, output, gate decisions, QA scenarios and the handoff marker on disk so a resumed session picks the run up where it stopped, and writing the run's Markdown report at the end. No page, no port, nothing rendered: the right surface for scheduled and unattended runs. Declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: delivery-dashboard
plugins.description: A run surface: the live dashboard a run is watched in. An MCP server implementing all three surface capability groups — lifecycle (open_dashboard, start_run, record_prompt, set_run_context, update_stage, finish_run, list_runs, get_run), render (render_diagram, render_markdown), and export (export_report) — with a run timeline carrying stage output, QA scenarios and their evidence, a Mermaid diagram viewer and a Markdown document viewer, and hook-captured tool and token telemetry. Rendered inline as an MCP App where the host supports it, served on 127.0.0.1 where it does not. Declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: fleet
plugins.description: The fan-out lane: a backlog turned into parallel work across sessions and worktrees — the one thing a flow may never do. fleet-issue-sweep triages a repository's open issues for relevance and for collision with work in flight, proposes the stale ones for closure, and dispatches up to five independent worker sessions, one issue and one worktree each, then waits them out and writes the brief. fleet-resolve-issue is what each worker runs: one issue to a pull request when the change proves itself, or to a parked worktree with a handoff brief when a human has to look. fleet-morning-brief re-reads a past sweep from its manifest and worker result files. An L1 extension over delivery: it owns no flow and holds no gate, and trades Personal Validation for a pull request nobody merges unread.

plugins.name: claude-desktop
plugins.description: The Claude host profile: it binds the delivery engine's six host slots to Claude's own files, paths, and capabilities — repo-instructions to CLAUDE.md, repo-flow-context to .claude/flow-context.md, model-override to the personal flow model-selection file, stage-delegation to sub-agents, surface to delivery-dashboard, pr-lane to the gh CLI — and ships the two procedures that belong to the host rather than to the engine: start, which brings the repository's own application up and opens it, and session-handoff, which packages a session into a brief the next one continues from. Declares no dependency: the flows themselves live in delivery, and a binding nothing reads is inert.

plugins.name: devbook
plugins.description: The devbook convention: .arc42, .domain, .tech, .design, and .ai knowledge folders of addressed Markdown chapters, each carrying a parseable meta block with status ladders, a shared approved rung, runnable test-case links, an opaque ext namespace a layered plugin keeps its own state in, and annotation fences that keep a review note in the chapter beside the passage it is about, compiled into derived _meta indexes and a reference-graph canvas. Ships bidirectional to-spec-<kind> and from-spec-<kind> converters between chapters and code, a versioned contract with runnable migrations, and enforcement tooling. Usable on its own: the per-folder flow-* procedures live in the devbook-flows bridge.

plugins.name: devbook-flows
plugins.description: The bridge between devbook and the delivery engine: five folder-specific flow-* procedures — flow-domain, flow-tech, flow-design, flow-arc42-content, flow-ai — that route a knowledge-folder change through the engine's staged phases, the Personal Validation gate, and whichever delivery surface is bound. Depends on both sides and is meaningless without either: devbook alone edits its folders directly under its instruction files, devbook plus delivery routes them through flow-fallback, and this plugin is what makes each folder its own flow.

plugins.name: devbook-collaboration
plugins.description: Review, comment, and hand-off workflows over devbook chapters. Requests a review and hands a chapter to a named reviewer, reviews one against its folder's rules and its evidence, records findings and the reviewer's verdict, runs the approval decision that writes devbook's own approved rung, and sweeps the adopted folders for what is awaiting whom and which approvals have gone stale. An L1 extension: every fact it remembers lives under ext.devbook-collaboration in the chapter's own meta block, so it adds no field to devbook's schema and needs no devbook release of its own.

plugins.name: architecture
plugins.description: Architecture documentation through the `architect` agent: arc42 sections, blueprints, architectural decision records, technical debt records, and C4, sequence, state-machine, and deployment diagrams. Fills the `architecture` role and the `spec` service a flow consults, and is usable on its own.

plugins.name: csharp-coding
plugins.description: C# .NET implementation through the `coding` agent: test-driven development, refactoring, code review and optimization, NuGet management, Aspire wiring, OpenTelemetry, and Azure SDK patterns. Fills the `implement` and `verify` services a flow runs its code stages through, and is usable on its own.

plugins.name: qa
plugins.description: Runtime QA validation through the `qa` and `qa-monitor` agents: run the app under Aspire, drive Playwright scenarios that record screenshot and video evidence, and keep log and trace monitoring active for the full session rather than checking once at the end. Fills the `qa` role and the `app.start` and `qa.run` services, and is usable on its own.

plugins.name: domain
plugins.description: Domain-Driven Design through the `domain` agent: bounded context discovery, ubiquitous language, domain model and interaction design, context mapping, and aggregate, domain-event-flow, and subdomain diagrams. Fills the `domain` role a flow consults, and is usable on its own. Holds no flow control: sequencing, approval, and delegation belong to whatever consults it.

plugins.name: ux
plugins.description: UX design through the `ux` agent: wireframes, user flows, design guidelines, and UI reviews, as SVG or Mermaid artifacts and structured Markdown. Fills the `ux` role a flow consults, and is usable on its own. Holds no flow control: sequencing, approval, and delegation belong to whatever consults it.

plugins.name: documentation
plugins.description: Documentation and profile artifacts through the `documentation` and `profile` agents: how-to guides, explanations, articles, proposals, ideas, and SVG infographics, plus GitHub, LinkedIn, and project profiles. Fills the `docs` role a flow consults, and is usable on its own.

plugins.name: spec-builder
plugins.description: Authoring the assets a plugin is made of, through the `spec-builder` agent and its five create-* skills: agents, skills, instruction files, hooks, and the two manifests. Carries the dual-host rules that let one authored copy load in both Claude Code and Copilot, and the conciseness budgets every asset here is held to.
